references.text: Cain killed his brother Abel—the first example of fratricide in the Bible, forming a parallel to Joseph's brothers who planned to kill him.
The brothers carry out the lie they planned in verse 20: they dip Joseph's coat in blood and tell their father that a wild animal has devoured him.
The brothers later acknowledge their guilt for what they planned against Joseph: they saw his distress as he pleaded with them, but they refused to listen.
The psalmist asks to be hidden from the secret plans of the wicked and their conspiracy, mirroring the brothers' plotting against Joseph.
A warning against those who plan to shed innocent blood and lie in ambush, parallel to the brothers' conspiracy against the innocent Joseph.
Jeremiah was thrown into a cistern (well), just as Joseph's brothers planned to throw him into a well—a strong typological parallel.
In the parable of the wicked tenants, the tenants kill the owner's son to seize the inheritance, mirroring the brothers' jealousy and their desire to eliminate Joseph.
Judas arranges to betray Jesus for silver coins, parallel to the brothers who later sold Joseph for twenty pieces of silver (Gen 37:28).
Stephen summarizes that the patriarchs sold Joseph into Egypt out of envy, but God was with him—a direct summary of the murder plot and its consequences.
A parallel conspiracy to destroy a man of God and erase his name/memory.
Direct narrative connection: Hatred for the dreams leads directly to the murder plot.
